I spoke to you previously about a number of things.
I have been developing a multi-tab interface for VS Code, modifying src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editor.ts, tabsTitleControl.ts, editorGroupView.ts, and editorPart.ts. I implemented a 'Save All' function using IWindowsMainService and IWorkingCopyService, global shortcuts in windowRegistry.ts, and state persistence in workbench.ts using onBeforeUnload and a DebouncedScheduler.

For cross-window tab dragging, I utilized ipcRenderer and ipcMain with a proxy window, resolving hit detection via setIgnoreMouseEvents and preventing flickering by setting hasShadow: false and backgroundColor: #00000000. I eliminated white flashes in workbench.ts by waiting for an editorInitialized event and handled tab detachment by passing dimensions via IPC to instantiate a new BrowserWindow, ensuring focus by calling focus() on the new instance after onWindowReady. I implemented refreshLayout() in tabList.ts, resolved a race condition in windowRegistry.ts, and fixed an 'Error: IPC channel closed' in lifecycle.ts by adding a promise-waiter for 'EditorSync'.

I updated serializable.ts and the TabModel interface in tabList.ts to include isPinned, added safety checks to editorGroup.ts, and integrated telemetry via telemetryService.ts. I validated IPC payloads in ipcHandler.ts using a strict schema validator and verified URI.file() for UNC path handling in paths.ts. To mitigate layout thrashing, I set pointer-events: none on the tab-drag-ghost in workbench-layout.css.

Following maintainer feedback, I refactored tab-tearing logic into a new TabManagerService (tabManager.ts), injecting IWindowService and IInstantiationService, and using an Emitter to expose an onDidTabDetach event. I addressed an 'IllegalStateException' in dnd.ts caused by rapid drag operations by implementing a promise-based init flow in TabManagerService and adding a guard clause to ensure drag-and-drop awaits service readiness. I also checked the isReadonly() state of the ITextEditorModel to ensure I only call focus if the model allows interaction.

I asked you for guidance on improving UX after drag-and-drop by ensuring the primary editor part is focused so the user can begin typing immediately. Per your advice, I implemented a hook to call focus() on the primary editor part within the new window. I have since squashed and pushed my changes, updated CHANGELOG.md, and verified that the opacity transition for the visual ghost image is properly scoped to the .tab-drag-ghost selector in tabs.css to ensure theme compatibility with workbench.ts. Finally, I confirmed that all tests passed, including the new testDragAndDropCancel suite, and verified that the memory profile shows no leaks when repeatedly tearing and canceling tabs. I have submitted the final diff to the maintainers.

I am prepared to document future progress, including specific library usage, class structures, and error handling, as we proceed.
